title: The Concept of Cognitive Dissonance
text:
Cognitive dissonance represents a state of mental discomfort that arises when an individual holds two or more conflicting cognitions (ideas, beliefs, values) or when behavior contradicts established beliefs. This psychological tension is inherently motivating, prompting the person to reduce the discrepancy and restore a sense of internal consistency.

The resolution process can occur in several ways: belief modification, behavioral changes, or, most commonly, the introduction of new consonant cognitions to rationalize the conflict. For example, acknowledging that an expensive purchase was wasteful while simultaneously emphasizing its unique features helps diminish the discomfort caused by perceived poor decision-making.

This theory has significant implications for understanding attitude change and resistance to persuasion, demonstrating how heavily people rely on internal consistency to maintain a stable self-image.
